claim: Mount Carillon does not appear in data/peaks.csv or data/collections/sps.csv. It is believed to be a real Sierra Peaks Section peak (Whitney region, near Mount Russell/Tulainyo Lake) but this project has not independently confirmed its SPS status, elevation, or GNIS coordinates. If added, its approach relative to Whitney Portal (and whether it shares Mount Russell's permit or needs its own) is also unconfirmed against any source -- treat this as a proposal to add the peak and determine its approach, not a confirmed fact.
resolution_notes: REJECTED 2026-09-13: the claim is false. Mount Carillon is present in data/peaks.csv, stored under the Sierra Peaks Section list's misspelling 'Mount Carillion'. scripts/merge_gnis.py has mapped that to the GNIS official spelling since the coordinates were merged, so the project always knew. The report was filed because `plan.py` answered 'not found' to the correct spelling, which was a lookup bug rather than a missing peak. Fixed: peaks.csv gains an `aliases` column carrying the GNIS name, and name resolution now matches on alias and on the list's formatting markers. Nothing was added to the dataset. Kept rather than deleted -- a ledger that quietly removes its own wrong entries is worth less than one that shows them.
